To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the standard pointparticle approach should be modified, to account for finite size, in simulations for particle-laden flows.
the fluid displaced due to particle presence is important for the accurate simulation of disperse flows.
the fluid displaced due to the finite size of the particles should be accounted for in the fluid phase continuity equation, in order to obtain correct particle behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical simulation of particle-laden gas flows in complex geometrical domains.
the development of numerical techniques to study complex particle-laden flows, in particular, the effect of finite size of the particles on the fluid-particle interaction and the overall flow field.
developing and testing numerical methods for simulating the flow of particles in fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite-size effects should be considered for all particle sizes and for all flow configurations, and the standard point-particles formulation is valid only for small particles.
the effect of finite size is important and should be accounted for in simulations of particle motion.
the finite-size formulation is necessary for accurate simulations of disperse flows, especially in the case of large particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite-size formulation is essential in predicting the correct fluid velocity and pressure fields.
the finite-size effects are important in the context of particle-laden flow simulations, and the point-particle approach is not valid in general.
finite-size effects are important in particle-laden flows with low volume fractions and/or large particle size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the finite-size effect should be considered when simulating particle-laden flows.
the finite-size of particles should be accounted for in simulations of particle–flow interactions in complex geometries.
the fluid displaced volume by the particles should be accounted for when simulating particle-laden flows.
